regulator.name: College of Medical Radiation and Imaging Technologists of Ontario

scope.quote: The practice of medical radiation and imaging technology is the use of ionizing radiation, electromagnetism, soundwaves and other prescribed forms of energy for the purposes of diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, the evaluation of images and data relating to the procedures and the assessment of an individual before, during and after the procedures.
scope.quoteSource: Medical Radiation and Imaging Technology Act, 2017, section 3
scope.plain: Radiation therapists use the therapeutic side of this: they plan and give radiation treatment, and check on the patient before, during and after each session. Treatments must be ordered by a physician.

exams.name: CAMRT certification exam (radiation therapy)
exams.by: Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists
exams.note: National exam. Open to graduates of an accredited radiation therapy program.

exams.name: Jurisprudence course and quiz
exams.note: Covers Ontario's laws and rules for the profession. Done as part of your registration application.

wage.note: Job Bank groups radiation therapists with radiographers and MRI technologists, so this figure covers all of them.

path.detail: Each program lists its own required courses. Check the program cards.
About 3 to 4 years. Some programs, like Michener–U of T, need a year of university first.
Complete the jurisprudence course, then start work as an MRT(T).

specializations.title: Advanced practice radiation therapist — APRT(T)
specializations.detail: A CAMRT certification for experienced therapists who take on advanced clinical roles.

specializations.title: Clinical Specialist Radiation Therapist (CSRT)
specializations.detail: An Ontario advanced role for radiation therapists, first introduced in 2006.

regulator.name: College of Medical Radiation and Imaging Technologists of Ontario

scope.quote: The practice of medical radiation and imaging technology is the use of ionizing radiation, electromagnetism, soundwaves and other prescribed forms of energy for the purposes of diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, the evaluation of images and data relating to the procedures and the assessment of an individual before, during and after the procedures.
scope.quoteSource: Medical Radiation and Imaging Technology Act, 2017, section 3
scope.plain: Sonographers use the soundwave part of this. They use ultrasound to make images of organs, blood vessels and babies before birth, check that the images answer the doctor's question, and look after the patient during the scan.

exams.name: Sonography Canada credentialing exams
exams.note: National exams for graduates of an accredited sonography program, in generalist, cardiac or vascular sonography.

exams.name: Jurisprudence course and quiz
exams.note: Covers Ontario's laws and rules for the profession. Done as part of your registration application.

path.detail: Each program lists its own required courses. Check the program cards.
A college advanced diploma or a joint university–college degree.
Complete the jurisprudence course, then start work as a DMS.

specializations.title: Cardiac or vascular sonography
specializations.detail: Sonography Canada offers separate credentials for generalist (CRGS), cardiac (CRCS) and vascular (CRVS) sonographers.

oversight.text: Paramedics in Ontario don't have a regulatory college. The Ministry of Health certifies them, and the medical director of a regional base hospital program authorizes the medical procedures each paramedic can do.

scope.quote: In Ontario, to be considered a paramedic who can perform controlled acts and other advanced medical procedures, an individual must: have the appropriate certificate from the Ministry of Health, be employed by a certified ambulance service, be authorized by the medical director of an Ontario regional base hospital program.
scope.quoteSource: Ontario Ministry of Health, Certification and patient care standards
scope.plain: What a paramedic can do depends on their level: primary care, advanced care or critical care. The exact procedures for each level are listed in Ontario Regulation 257/00 under the Ambulance Act.

exams.name: AEMCA exam (Advanced Emergency Medical Care Assistant)
exams.note: The provincial entry-to-practice exam for primary care paramedics. Open to graduates of an approved PCP program.

wage.note: Figure shown is for primary care paramedics.

path.detail: Each program lists its own required courses. Check the program cards.
Usually a 2-year college diploma, or a joint university–college degree.
Join a certified ambulance service and be authorized by a regional base hospital.

specializations.title: Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP)
specializations.detail: Further training that adds advanced procedures. You need an AEMCA certificate to apply for the ACP exam.

specializations.title: Critical care and flight paramedic
specializations.detail: Critical Care Paramedic and flight paramedic (aerophysiology) training is offered by Ornge, Ontario's air ambulance service.

scope.quote: The practice of nursing is the promotion of health and the assessment of, the provision of care for and the treatment of health conditions by supportive, preventive, therapeutic, palliative and rehabilitative means in order to attain or maintain optimal function.
scope.plain: Registered nurses assess patients, give treatments and medications, teach patients and families, and coordinate care with the rest of the team, from preventing illness to end-of-life care.

exams.name: NCLEX-RN
exams.note: The registration exam for registered nurses.

exams.name: Jurisprudence exam
exams.note: Multiple-choice exam on the laws, rules and standards for nurses in Ontario.

wage.nocTitle: Registered nurses and registered psychiatric nurses

path.detail: Each program lists its own required courses. Check the program cards.
Pass the jurisprudence exam, then start work as an RN.

specializations.title: Nurse practitioner
specializations.detail: A protected title in Ontario. RNs reach it through further graduate education and registration in CNO's Extended Class.

regulator.name: College of Medical Radiation and Imaging Technologists of Ontario

scope.quote: The practice of medical radiation and imaging technology is the use of ionizing radiation, electromagnetism, soundwaves and other prescribed forms of energy for the purposes of diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, the evaluation of images and data relating to the procedures and the assessment of an individual before, during and after the procedures.
scope.quoteSource: Medical Radiation and Imaging Technology Act, 2017, section 3
scope.plain: MRI technologists use the electromagnetism part of this. They screen patients for safety, run MRI scans, check image quality, and can give contrast dye by injection when a physician orders it.

exams.name: CAMRT certification exam (magnetic resonance)
exams.by: Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists
exams.note: National exam. Open to graduates of an accredited MRI program.

exams.name: Jurisprudence course and quiz
exams.note: Covers Ontario's laws and rules for the profession. Done as part of your registration application.

wage.note: Job Bank groups MRI technologists with radiographers and radiation therapists, so this figure covers all of them.

path.detail: Each program lists its own required courses. Check the program cards.
A college diploma or advanced diploma.
Complete the jurisprudence course, then start work as an MRT(MR).
